team_text:
We would like to register an AI use case. It is called TalentRank. The Head of Talent Acquisition owns it. It is a module of our vendor applicant tracking system. The vendor is an international HR software company. It is in production for graduate hiring. It reads CVs submitted for graduate and branch roles, scores each candidate against the job requirements and ranks them. Recruiters shortlist the top-ranked candidates for interviews; candidates below the cut-off are rarely looked at. It is an HR recruitment use. Not for senior or internal promotions. Ten recruiters in Talent Acquisition, trained by the vendor. Job candidates applying to the Bank. Yes, each score is about one candidate. About 8,000 CVs a month during graduate season. Candidates with disabilities or career gaps could be disadvantaged; recruiters can manually add them. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. It recommends a ranking; recruiters decide whom to interview. Recruiters review the ranked list and can add any candidate to the shortlist. Candidates can ask HR for feedback and a manual review. CV text, education, work history and assessment test scores. Personal data of candidates. It uses no biometric data. The vendor model is pre-trained and fine-tuned on our last three years of hiring outcomes. We checked that historical hires were not dominated by a few universities and removed university names from features. Vendor cloud in the EU. A vendor NLP ranking model. It does not generate any text, image or other content. No, candidates do not interact with it. Reads from the careers portal and writes rankings to the applicant tracking system. It agrees with recruiter shortlists 78% of the time on a back-test. We compared shortlisting rates by gender and city; female shortlisting was 4 points lower and we adjusted the cut-off. It shows which requirements each candidate matched. Vendor security certification reviewed. Quarterly shortlisting and fairness reports reviewed by HR. HR can switch off ranking and screen manually. Rankings and recruiter actions are logged for three years. The careers portal says applications are screened with automated tools. Procurement and IT risk completed due diligence and the contract includes audit rights. Labour law and data protection expectations apply.

obligations.title: AI literacy
obligations.text: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: Penalties
obligations.text: Up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited practices; up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other obligations; up to EUR 7.5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to authorities.

obligations.title: AI literacy
obligations.text: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Provider obligations and quality management system
obligations.text: Providers ensure compliance with Section 2, have a quality management system, keep documentation and logs, undergo conformity assessment (Art. 43), draw up an EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), affix CE marking (Art. 48), register (Art. 49), take corrective actions (Art. 20) and demonstrate conformity on request.

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Conformity assessment
obligations.text: High-risk systems undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market; for most Annex III systems this is internal control (Annex VI).

obligations.title: Registration
obligations.text: Providers (and public-authority deployers) register Annex III high-risk systems in the EU database before placing them on the market or putting them into service.

obligations.title: Post-market monitoring
obligations.text: Providers establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the risk, actively collecting and analysing data on performance throughout the lifetime.

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: Penalties
obligations.text: Up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited practices; up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other obligations; up to EUR 7.5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to authorities.

obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Conformity assessment
obligations.text: High-risk systems undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market; for most Annex III systems this is internal control (Annex VI).

obligations.title: Registration
obligations.text: Providers (and public-authority deployers) register Annex III high-risk systems in the EU database before placing them on the market or putting them into service.

obligations.title: Post-market monitoring
obligations.text: Providers establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the risk, actively collecting and analysing data on performance throughout the lifetime.

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: Penalties
obligations.text: Up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited practices; up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other obligations; up to EUR 7.5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to authorities.

team_text: We would like to register an AI use case. It is called CarePrice. The Head of Bancatakaful owns it. It is provided by our takaful operator partner. The vendor is our partner takaful operator's actuarial platform. In production. It assesses each customer's health risk from a medical questionnaire and sets the contribution rate for individual health takaful plans sold through our branches. Branch staff quote the contribution and the partner's underwriter can accept, load or decline the cover. Health takaful (insurance) pricing and risk assessment. Not for group plans. Bancatakaful sales officers and partner underwriters, trained by the partner. Individual customers applying for health takaful. Yes, pricing is per individual. About 3,000 quotes a month. Older customers and people with chronic conditions pay more; underwriters review declines. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. It recommends a price; underwriters approve. Partner underwriters review loaded and declined cases and can override the price. Customers can request a review by the partner's underwriting team and complain to the Bank. Medical questionnaire answers, age, occupation and sum covered. Health data, which is special-category personal data. It uses no biometric data. The partner's claims experience data. The partner checked representativeness by age band and region. Partner's onshore data centre. Generalised linear model with machine learning risk adjustments. It does not generate any text, image or other content. Nobody interacts with it directly; it runs in the background. Reads the questionnaire from our branch sales system and writes quotes back. Loss ratio prediction error within 5% on the back-test. Pricing differences by gender and region were reviewed by the partner's actuary. Price breakdown by risk factor is shown to the customer. Partner pen-tested the platform. Quarterly loss ratio and pricing reviews. Partner notifies us within 24 hours; quotes revert to the manual rate table. Quotes and overrides are logged for ten years. The quote explains that automated risk assessment is used. Due diligence completed and the bancatakaful agreement covers data, audit and incidents. A data protection and fairness impact assessment was completed. SECP takaful rules and SBP bancassurance guidelines apply.

obligations.title: AI literacy
obligations.text: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: Penalties
obligations.text: Up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited practices; up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other obligations; up to EUR 7.5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to authorities.

team_text:
Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called BranchGuard. The Head of Physical Security owns it. Vendor product. A local security systems integrator using a foreign face recognition engine. It runs face recognition on branch CCTV and matches everyone who enters against a watchlist of known fraudsters. Not for marketing or attendance. Branch managers and security guards. Every customer and visitor entering the pilot branches. Yes, matches concern individuals. About 50,000 visitors a month. Not assessed. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. It recommends; staff decide what to do. The branch manager checks the match image before acting. Customers can complain to the branch. CCTV video and the watchlist photos. Facial biometric data. The vendor's pre-trained engine. Not done. On local servers in each branch. Deep learning face recognition. It does not generate any text, image or other content. Reads CCTV feeds and writes alerts to the security console. The vendor quotes 98% accuracy. Shows the matched watchlist photo and similarity score. Vendor tested; not independently tested. Monthly alert review by Physical Security. Security can switch off matching per branch. Alerts are kept for one year. A small sign says CCTV is in operation. Basic vendor onboarding checks were done. Not checked yet.

obligations.title: AI literacy
obligations.text: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: Penalties
obligations.text: Up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited practices; up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other obligations; up to EUR 7.5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to authorities.

team_text:
Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called CardShield. The Head of Fraud Risk owns it. It is a vendor fraud platform. A global payments fraud vendor. In production. It scores every debit and credit card transaction for fraud in real time. Fraud detection. Not for credit decisions or AML reporting. The fraud operations team. Cardholders and the merchants they pay. About 4 million transactions a month. Elderly customers abroad are more often blocked; they can call the 24-hour line. Cardholders sometimes travel in the EU but no output is used there by us. High-risk transactions are declined and cards blocked automatically without human review. Fraud operations review blocked cards within 30 minutes during business hours and can unblock them. Customers can call the 24-hour helpline to confirm the transaction and unblock the card. Transaction details, merchant data, device and location data. Personal financial data. It uses no biometric data. Vendor cloud in Singapore. Vendor neural network fraud model. It does not generate any text, image or other content. Nobody interacts with it directly; it runs in the background. Reads card authorisations from the card switch and writes decline and block instructions back to it. Fraud detection rate of 72% at a false-positive ratio of 8 to 1. We have checked block rates by age band; customers over 65 are blocked 1.4 times more often. Top risk factors per alert. Vendor is PCI DSS certified and pen-tested. Daily fraud and false-positive dashboards; monthly model review with the vendor. We can switch to rules-only mode within minutes. All scores and decisions are logged for seven years. Customers receive an SMS when a transaction is declined. Full vendor due diligence and an SBP-compliant outsourcing contract. A data protection impact assessment was completed. SBP cloud outsourcing framework and payment card rules apply.

obligations.title: AI literacy
obligations.text: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Transparency: emotion recognition and biometric categorisation
obligations.text: Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems inform the natural persons exposed to them of the operation of the system and process personal data in accordance with data protection law.

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: Penalties
obligations.text: Up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for prohibited practices; up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other obligations; up to EUR 7.5 million or 1% for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to authorities.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

obligations.title: AI literacy
obligations.text: Providers and deployers take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy of staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf.

obligations.title: Risk management system
obligations.text: A continuous, iterative risk management process across the lifecycle: identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights; estimate risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; evaluate post-market data; adopt targeted risk management measures; test the system; give specific consideration to persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).

obligations.title: Data and data governance
obligations.text: Training, validation and testing data subject to governance practices covering design choices, data collection processes and origin, preparation operations, assumptions, availability and suitability, examination for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, measures to detect, prevent and mitigate such biases, and identification of data gaps. Data must be relevant, sufficiently representative and as free of errors and complete as possible. Art. 10(5) allows processing special categories of personal data strictly for bias detection and correction, with safeguards.

obligations.title: Technical documentation
obligations.text: Technical documentation drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date: general description, intended purpose, development process, design specifications, data requirements, human oversight measures, validation and testing procedures and metrics, risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.title: Record-keeping
obligations.text: Technical capability for automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, enabling identification of risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

obligations.title: Transparency and information to deployers
obligations.text: Designed so deployers can interpret output and use it appropriately; accompanied by instructions for use with the provider's identity, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, known or foreseeable circumstances leading to risks, performance regarding specific persons or groups, input data specifications, human oversight measures, expected lifetime and maintenance, and log collection mechanisms.

obligations.title: Human oversight
obligations.text: Designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Oversight measures enable the assigned persons to: understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation; remain aware of automation bias; correctly interpret output; decide not to use, disregard, override or reverse the output; intervene or interrupt through a stop button or similar procedure.

obligations.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.text: Appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, performing consistently throughout the lifecycle. Accuracy levels and metrics declared in instructions for use. Resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies; feedback loops addressed; resilient against attempts to alter use or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks).

obligations.title: Provider obligations and quality management system
obligations.text: Providers ensure compliance with Section 2, have a quality management system, keep documentation and logs, undergo conformity assessment (Art. 43), draw up an EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), affix CE marking (Art. 48), register (Art. 49), take corrective actions (Art. 20) and demonstrate conformity on request.

obligations.title: Responsibilities along the value chain
obligations.text: A deployer or other third party becomes a provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk system so that it becomes high-risk.

obligations.title: Deployer obligations
obligations.text: Deployers: use the system according to instructions (26(1)); assign human oversight to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority (26(2)); ensure input data under their control is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor operation and inform the provider, and suspend use if it presents a risk; report serious incidents (26(5)); keep automatically generated logs for at least six months (26(6)); inform workers' representatives before use in the workplace (26(7)); inform natural persons that they are subject to a high-risk system that makes or assists decisions about them (26(11)).

obligations.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment
obligations.text: Before deployment, bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of Annex III 5(b) (creditworthiness) and 5(c) (life and health insurance) systems perform an assessment of: the deployer's processes using the system; period and frequency of use; categories of natural persons and groups likely to be affected; specific risks of harm to them; human oversight measures; measures to be taken if risks materialise, including internal governance and complaint mechanisms.

obligations.title: Conformity assessment
obligations.text: High-risk systems undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market; for most Annex III systems this is internal control (Annex VI).

obligations.title: Registration
obligations.text: Providers (and public-authority deployers) register Annex III high-risk systems in the EU database before placing them on the market or putting them into service.

obligations.title: Post-market monitoring
obligations.text: Providers establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the risk, actively collecting and analysing data on performance throughout the lifetime.

obligations.title: Reporting of serious incidents
obligations.text: Serious incidents are reported to the market surveillance authority immediately after a causal link is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (shorter deadlines for widespread infringements or death).

obligations.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
obligations.text: A person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of output from an Annex III high-risk system, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, has the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.

It assesses whether employees of our payroll clients are eligible for a salary advance and recommends the maximum advance amount. Payroll banking officers approve or decline each salary advance request using the recommendation. Consumer credit (salary advance financing). Not for other financing products. Five payroll banking officers, trained internally. Salaried individuals working for our payroll clients. Yes, it assesses individual employees. About 1,500 requests a month. Low-paid workers; advances are capped at 50% of net salary. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. It recommends; officers approve. Officers review each request and can change the amount; they override about 10%. Employees can ask their HR focal person to request a manual review. Approval rates compared by gender and salary band; gaps under 3 points. Reason codes per recommendation. Tested on missing payroll months. Monthly default and override monitoring. Officers revert to manual policy rules. Logged for ten years. Employees are told the advance uses an automated eligibility score. AI impact assessment completed in April 2026. team_text:
Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called AskAmana. The Head of Customer Service owns it. We built it on a third-party large language model API. The model is a commercial LLM accessed through an API provider. In production on WhatsApp. It answers customers' questions about our products, fees and branch timings on WhatsApp, using only our published product documents. Customer service. It must not give account-specific, financial or Shariah rulings advice. Customers use it directly; the digital service team manages it. Customers and members of the public who message us on WhatsApp. About 80,000 conversations a month. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. Customer questions and our published product documents. Customers' phone numbers and messages, which are personal data. It uses no biometric data. It is a pre-trained model; we do not train it, we ground it on our documents. Messages go to the model provider's API in the United States under a zero-retention agreement. A large language model with retrieval over our documents. Yes, it generates text answers. Yes, customers chat with it directly on WhatsApp. Reads from the product document store; writes chat transcripts to the CRM. On 500 test questions it answered 91% correctly and refused 6% appropriately. We red-teamed it with 300 prompt-injection and abuse prompts. Answers are grounded only on approved documents, an output filter blocks account advice and abusive content, and every answer cites a document. Weekly accuracy sampling and a monthly hallucination review. Digital service can switch WhatsApp to human agents immediately. The first message tells customers they are talking to an AI assistant. The API provider was assessed by IT risk; the contract covers zero retention and incident notice.

team_text:
Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called ReplyAssist. The Head of Complaints Management owns it. Built on a third-party LLM API. A commercial LLM API provider. It drafts written replies to customer complaints, which agents edit and send to customers by email. It does not decide the complaint outcome; agents decide and send the final reply. Customer service and complaints. It must not decide refunds or compensation. Thirty complaints agents. Customers who complain. Yes, replies go to individual customers, though it decides nothing about them. About 9,000 replies a month. Vulnerable complainants are flagged for senior handling. Agents approve every reply before it is sent. Complaint text and case notes. Customer personal data in complaint text, with CNIC and account numbers masked before the API. It uses no biometric data. Pre-trained model with our reply templates in the prompt. API provider in the United States, zero retention. Large language model. No, only agents use it. Agents accept 70% of drafts with minor edits; QA scores unchanged. Masking and prompt-injection tests done. Masking, a template library and agent approval of every reply. Monthly QA sampling of sent replies. Agents revert to templates. Replies state that they were prepared with AI assistance and reviewed by an agent. API provider assessed. SBP complaint handling rules.

Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called DevPilot. The Chief Technology Officer owns it. It is a third-party coding assistant built on a large language model API. A commercial AI coding assistant provider. In production for the IT department. It suggests code completions and explains code to our software developers inside their editor. Internal productivity for software development. Only our developers use it; no customers are affected directly. No, it does not produce outputs about people. It only suggests code; developers decide. Source code and developer prompts; no customer data. It uses no biometric data. Pre-trained by the provider; our code is not used for training under the contract. Provider's cloud in the United States; code snippets are not retained. Large language model for code. Developers interact with it in their editor. Integrated into developer editors; it cannot change production systems. Developers accept about 30% of suggestions; security scans show no increase in vulnerabilities. Secrets scanning blocks credentials in prompts; static analysis runs on all code. Code review, static analysis and a licence filter for suggested code. Quarterly review of usage and security scan results. IT can revoke licences immediately. IT risk assessed the provider and the contract excludes training on our code. team_text:
Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called ComplaintRouter. The Head of Complaints Management owns it. Built in-house. In production. It reads the text of written complaints, classifies the product and topic, scores the sentiment of the text, and routes the complaint to the right team. It only routes complaints; the outcome is decided by complaint handlers. Customer service. Not for deciding complaint outcomes. Customers who submit written complaints. Yes, each complaint belongs to a customer, but it decides nothing about them. About 12,000 complaints a month. Complaints mentioning hardship are routed to the vulnerable customer desk. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. Routing is automatic. Complaint text. Customer personal data in complaint text. None; it uses written text only. Two years of labelled complaints. It does not generate any text, image or other content. Nobody interacts with it directly; it runs in the background. Reads from the complaints portal; writes queue assignments. Tested on Roman Urdu and mixed-language text. Monthly re-route rate review. Manual triage fallback. Not applicable; it does not decide anything about customers.
1. Routing accuracy 91%; sentiment agreement with QA 84%.
2. Complaints team.
3. Onshore.
4. Fine-tuned text classifier.
5. SBP complaint handling rules.

team_text:
Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called SMEScore. The Head of SME Banking owns it. In production. It scores the credit risk of incorporated companies, private limited companies only, applying for working capital financing, from their audited financial statements. SME relationship managers and the credit committee use the score when deciding company financing. SME and corporate lending to companies. SME credit analysts. Incorporated companies applying for financing. No, it scores companies, not individuals. No personal data; company data only. It uses no biometric data. Eight years of SME financing outcomes. Logistic regression scorecard. It does not generate any text, image or other content. Nobody interacts with it directly; it runs in the background. Reads from the credit workflow; writes scores back. Gini 0.60. Tested on missing financials. Quarterly validation. Analysts revert to the manual rating. SBP prudential regulations for SME financing.
1. Built in-house.
2. It recommends; the credit committee decides.
3. Audited financial statements, company bureau data and account conduct.
4. Onshore.

Registration request for a new AI use case. It is called AMLSentinel. The Head of Financial Crime Compliance owns it. Vendor AML platform. A financial crime compliance software vendor. In production. It scores transactions and customers for money laundering risk and raises alerts. AML analysts investigate alerts and decide whether to file a suspicious transaction report. AML and financial crime compliance. Not for credit or marketing. Customers and their transaction counterparties. Yes, alerts concern individual customers. About 3 million transactions a month and 1,500 alerts. Not specifically. No output is used in the EU and no affected people are in the EU. It only raises alerts; analysts decide. Every alert is reviewed by an analyst and a supervisor approves any report. Not applicable; reports are confidential by law. Transactions, KYC profile and counterparty data. It uses no biometric data. Vendor scenarios tuned on our alert history. Data quality checks run daily. On-premises. Rules plus a machine learning alert prioritisation model. Nobody interacts with it directly; it runs in the background. Reads from core banking; writes alerts to the case management tool. Alert rates by region reviewed annually. Each alert lists the triggered scenarios. Annual independent model validation. Not applicable (tipping-off rules). Vendor due diligence completed. SBP AML/CFT regulations and the FMU reporting requirements.
